newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police to prosecute party leader - media.
newsitem.headline: Indian police to prosecute party leader - media.

text.p: Indian federal police have decided to prosecute the leader of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's political party and a government minister in a corruption investigation, state television and news agencies said on Sunday.

Doordarshan Television said Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) director Joginder Singh ordered the prosecution of Laloo Prasad Yadav, president of the Janata Dal party and chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, in a probe into the use of state animal welfare funds.
The 10 billion rupee ($280 million) "animal fodder" scandal involved the alleged siphoning of state funds from the scheme.
"The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) today decided to prosecute the Janata Dal president and Bihar chief minister, Mr Laloo Prasad Yadav," the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Doordarshan and PTI said Singh issued the prosecution orders after considering evidence. They did not say whether CBI would charge those it would be prosecuting.
Prosecution involves initiation of legal proceedings but this may not lead to criminal charges being brought.
Doordarshan and PTI said junior Rural Areas and Employment Minister Chandradeo Prasad Varma was among 56 people including politicians and bureaucrats who were due to be prosecuted.
PTI quoted Varma, who was appointed junior minister by Gujral last week, as denying any involvement in the scandal.
The news agency quoted Yadav as saying he had no knowledge of the CBI's decision to institute legal proceedings against him. "I do not know the details," he told PTI in the Bihar capital Patna.

In the past Yadav has repeatedly denied involvement in the scandal but said some officials in Bihar may have illegally taken money from the fund. Earlier this year, Yadav said he would prefer to be dismissed as Bihar chief minister than to resign.

Janata Dal is the biggest party in Gujral's 15-party United Front coalition. Both Gujral, who assumed power on April 21, and his ousted predecessor, former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, are Janata Dal members.
